candidates.label: yB (B only: second b/d capture with order flag + own lattice for the second captured b/d)
candidates.change: rev0 B zombie_entry rewritten (B startup, phoenix_init and worker unchanged). Built on A027 xyB. Captured zom20a (CX!=0): reads [4A19h] xor CCCCh as INT87 start (unset cell = DI 0 = rev0), bp 2000h. Captured b/d (CX=0): lea bp,[bx+0FDh]; xor bp,0CCCCh; xchg [4A19h],bp publishes its base+100h in the same instruction slot as xyB and returns the old cell value. First b/d (old = CCCCh): searches EB F9 CC CC backward from its own base+100h (below its own tails), replacement jmp [4A17h], bp 3400h. Second b/d (cell already set): rev0's 0E070E17 -> CC counter-bomb from DI 0, then phoenix with bp 9400h (own lattice point, never the same anchor as the first). Charge budget: A (zom20a), B (top tail), zom20a, each captured b/d = 1 INT87 each; with no early tail consumer (k=0) X needs 2 and Y 2 more = 5 > 4, so Y is only reachable when an opponent consumed X+165h (k=1).

threatFindings.threat: Charge budget allows capturing the lower zom20b/d (Y) in the common case.
threatFindings.evidence: Static (dis86 of zom20b/zom20d): four complete loop copies with tails at +11Ah/+133h/+14Ch/+165h, byte-identical, plus a truncated 5th copy at +16Bh (ends FE 0F, no tail); entry jmp 0139h makes +14Ch live. b and d differ only in the mov di immediate (12 26 vs 26 12) outside the loop, so no 4-byte pattern selects a live tail. Top-down needs 2 charges per zombie; with A, B, zom20a and the captured X (4 charges) and zom20a needing 1, k=0 needs 5. Only k=1 (an opponent consumed X+165h) leaves enough charges.
threatFindings.impact: Y capture limited to k=1 battles; measured value small (yB - yC +0.0044 on screen, 8 cohorts changed).

threatFindings.threat: A027 xyB loss came from the second captured b/d sharing the first's anchor / repeating the b/d search.
threatFindings.evidence: Same cohort set as A027 evtia (identical base 0.6924): yB 0.6969 (epuig, +0.0045) vs xyB 0.6267 (-0.066), ctl 0.6889, xyK 0.6726. yB differs from xyB only in the second-b/d path (counter-bomb + bp 9400h instead of b/d search + bp 3400h); which of the two parts matters is not separated.
threatFindings.impact: about +0.07 on those cohorts relative to xyB; makes multi-b/d capture non-harmful

threatFindings.threat: Several b/d zombies stolen through [5D13h] from b01d/e1p4/m050 all run rev0's b/d path on the same band+3400h anchor and waste or kill each other.
threatFindings.evidence: Effect verified: threat 7f4zg (fresh mixAll b01d+e1p4+m050) yB +0.254 [0.185,0.322] 12/0; screen sstrong-1 +0.311 and sstrong-5 +0.171 in both yB (vnmqe) and the control yC (u5bnq), so it does not depend on Y capture. Mechanism (anchor collision vs first-b/d search below itself) is a hypothesis: not traced.
threatFindings.impact: large against the m050/b01d hook lineage (strong group); 2025 group neutral (+0.006 / -0.002)

threatFindings.evidence: In yB the counter-bomb is kept only for the second captured b/d; the first b/d spends its charge on the search below itself. Screen 2025 group +0.006 (vnmqe), consistent with B052 (counter-bomb worth nothing measurable).
